reference_traces.rationale: The reviewer identified the feedforward lidar-and-reanalysis approach for CCN and ABS as a novel application in this domain; the final paper specifies the corresponding collocated training paradigm.

The reviewer questioned whether aircraft-trained models transfer to satellite observations. The final paper still presents simulated, noise-added UV observations and states that actual ATLID error characteristics determine prediction errors.

The reviewer described the use of lidar, in situ, and reanalysis data to predict the two higher-level aerosol properties; the final paper documents the four-campaign collocated dataset and the prediction targets.
The reviewer regarded the reported results as promising. The final paper reports held-out HSRL-2 performance and the improvement obtained by adding temperature and relative-humidity predictors.

Reviewers continued to challenge global representativeness because training data are dominated by ACTIVATE and did not establish coverage of unseen input space. The final paper confirms the imbalance, absence of a global climatology, and remaining sparse aerosol-type-specific regions.

The reviewer found that comparison of ML test errors with physics-based retrieval uncertainty was not like-for-like. The final paper expressly acknowledges that the two uncertainty sets differ and that future satellite applications require a fuller uncertainty assessment.

The reviewer highlighted low-value biases and their relevance to clean conditions. The final paper improves CCN through weighting but retains equal ABS weighting because weighting worsened overall ABS error, leaving limited clean-condition performance as a constraint.

The reviewer requested evidence that models can generalize beyond the field campaigns and noted unaddressed satellite-system differences. The final paper identifies actual satellite error characteristics and collocated observations as determinants of performance.
Audit-only: concerns about missing collocation and measurement-processing detail were addressed by added methods describing collocation, sampling, and instrument uncertainty.

Audit-only: the request for training, validation, and hyperparameter code was addressed by adding the ML algorithm and selected hyperparameters; the final paper states that custom code and data are available.

limiting_points.suggested_action: Frame satellite use as a prospective application until validation against actual satellite observations and their system-specific errors is available.
limiting_points.text: The contribution is a lidar-based retrieval paradigm, but its satellite extension remains unvalidated: the ATLID analysis uses airborne UV observations with added noise, and the final paper states that actual satellite error characteristics will determine prediction error.

supporting_points.suggested_action: Retain the distinction between the demonstrated collocated-aircraft paradigm and future system-specific retraining.
supporting_points.text: The work applies fully connected neural networks trained on collocated lidar and in situ observations, with reanalysis predictors, to estimate vertically resolved CCN and aerosol absorption—properties not traditionally derived from lidar alone.

questions.suggested_action: Specify a prospective validation protocol using actual satellite observations and independent collocated airborne or in situ reference measurements, including systematics and coverage differences.
questions.text: What validation framework will test transfer to actual satellite lidar data, including instrument systematics, observing geometry, resolution, coverage, and uncertainty sources not represented by the noise-added proxy?

strengths.suggested_action: Preserve the explicit scope of the four-campaign collocated training and testing design.
strengths.text: The study grounds the paradigm in HSRL-2 observations collocated with in situ CCN and absorption measurements across four airborne campaigns, with defined sampling and collocation procedures.

strengths.suggested_action: Report the configuration-specific metrics alongside the contribution claim.
strengths.text: For complete airborne HSRL-2 data, adding ERA5 temperature and relative humidity improves reported mean relative errors from 22% to 13% for CCN and from 25% to 21% for aerosol absorption.

summary.text: The paper presents a machine-learning paradigm that uses lidar observations, collocated in situ measurements, and reanalysis predictors to estimate CCN and aerosol absorption. The final manuscript documents strong configuration-specific airborne test performance and added methodological detail, while its central limits remain the heavily imbalanced campaign data, incomplete evidence for global or satellite transfer, and non-comparable uncertainty bases for ML and physics-based retrievals.

weaknesses.suggested_action: Quantify generalization with held-out-campaign and input-space coverage analyses, and limit claims to conditions supported by those tests.
weaknesses.text: The training distribution remains strongly concentrated in one campaign (96% of CCN and 76% of absorption data), and the paper acknowledges both the lack of a global CCN/ABS climatology and remaining aerosol-type-specific data insufficiencies. Distributional comparison at one continental site does not establish global representativeness or coverage of unseen lidar input space.

weaknesses.suggested_action: Avoid quantitative superiority claims across retrieval classes unless uncertainty components are evaluated on a common basis.
weaknesses.text: The comparison with physics-based retrievals is not directly comparable: the paper states that physics-based uncertainties include parametric, structural, forward-model, and measurement components, whereas the ML errors mainly reflect suborbital data and algorithm uncertainty. Thus reported ML test errors do not by themselves establish retrieval preference.

weaknesses.suggested_action: Provide condition-stratified uncertainty for both targets and clearly delimit interpretations in sparse clean-condition regimes.
weaknesses.text: Clean-condition bias is only partly mitigated. Triple weighting improves CCN predictions, but the analogous ABS weighting was not adopted because it increased overall ABS error; sparse low-value regimes therefore remain a performance limitation.

revision_ledger.residual_summary: Methods now state the collocation criteria, resolution, sample counts, and measurement uncertainties; this is retained as resolved audit history rather than a final review point.

The final paper identifies selected hyperparameters and states that custom code, data, and a reproduction Readme are available; this is retained as resolved audit history rather than a final review point.
